namadgi-national-park-1.name: Gibraltar Falls
namadgi-national-park-1.bio: Waterfall with a drop of over 50 m, with a lookout, barbecue and picnic area off Corin Road.
namadgi-national-park-1.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap waterway=waterfall (nominatim), HIGH; moved ~7.6 km from the placement point, which was the Wikivoyage listing coordinate (-35.5375,148.878), a wrong location
namadgi-national-park-1.notes: Wikivoyage Namadgi lists it under See (Corin Rd, Paddys River; drop over 50 m); lookout/barbecue/picnic from Wikivoyage Tuggeranong and Country ACT via the placement draft. Wikivoyage states Namadgi has no fees or permits. Visit time is an estimate.

namadgi-national-park-2.name: Booroomba Rocks
namadgi-national-park-2.bio: Walk to granite tors and a cliff edge on Booroomba Rocks Road, also a rock-climbing site.
namadgi-national-park-2.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap natural=peak node "Booroomba Rocks peak" (way 8047339456), within 70 m of the Wikipedia coordinates (HIGH); 0.7 km from placement point. Lies on the walk between car park and cliff edge, about 300 m from the route midpoint (OSM has no route relation)
namadgi-national-park-2.notes: Wikivoyage Do lists it as a trail through rocks (says 4 km); the Parks ACT walking tracks page (draft) gives 2.5 km return; bio avoids the distance. Visit time is an estimate.

namadgi-national-park-3.name: Orroral Homestead
namadgi-national-park-3.bio: Hut from the 1860s, the oldest in Namadgi and among the best conserved, with signs on pastoral life.
namadgi-national-park-3.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap way 583614115 Orroral Homestead (tourism=alpine_hut, building), MEDIUM; agrees with the Wikivoyage listing within 20 m. The Commons photo median (LOW, 1.2 km off, at the tracking station) was rejected
namadgi-national-park-3.notes: Wikivoyage Namadgi: easy walk for those at Orroral Campground; informative signs inside. Opening hours not stated by any source I could read; hut is open-air heritage site, 'Open 24 hours' is an assumption: unverified.

namadgi-national-park-4.name: Honeysuckle Creek Tracking Station
namadgi-national-park-4.bio: Former NASA Apollo tracking station site, believed to have first televised Armstrong's moon step, with signs on what stood here.
namadgi-national-park-4.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap node 4374907087 "Honeysuckle Creek Former Space Tracking Station" (tourism=attraction), MEDIUM; within 5 m of the Wikipedia/Wikivoyage coordinates (HIGH); 25 m from placement
namadgi-national-park-4.notes: Wikivoyage Namadgi: operated 1967-1981, 26-metre dish, little remains, plenty of information on what stood there. Access is by Apollo Road: unverified hours (assumed open access).

namadgi-national-park-5.name: Yankee Hat
namadgi-national-park-5.bio: Aboriginal rock painting of a kangaroo, dingos, emus and humans, reached on foot from Old Boboyan Road.
namadgi-national-park-5.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap node 800055143 "Yankee Hat Rock Art Site" (historic=archaeological_site, tourism=attraction), MEDIUM; on the Yankee Hat Walking Track. NOT the Yankee Hat peak (-35.755,148.935, Wikivoyage), which is ~1.7 km west
namadgi-national-park-5.notes: Wikivoyage Namadgi: mountain 1,441 m with an Aboriginal rock painting (kangaroo, dingos, emus, humans, echidna or turtle). Walking track exists in OSM (Yankee Hat Walking Track from Yankee Hat Carpark); length and time unverified.

namadgi-national-park-6.name: Bimberi Peak
namadgi-national-park-6.bio: The highest point in the ACT at 1,911 m, in the remote Bimberi area of Namadgi.
namadgi-national-park-6.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap natural=peak "Bimberi Peak" (nominatim), MEDIUM; within 25 m of Wikivoyage (-35.65926,148.79056) and 210 m of Wikipedia
namadgi-national-park-6.notes: Wikivoyage lists it as Mount Bimberi, highest in the ACT at 1,911 m. A summit hike: pinned on the summit; route length, access and the 6-10 hr visit range are unverified estimates.

namadgi-national-park-7.name: Settlers Track
namadgi-national-park-7.bio: 6 km loop from Boboyan Road through pastoral sites, with a 9 km option to Waterhole Hut.
namadgi-national-park-7.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap node 574151648 "Brayshaws Hut parking" (amenity=parking), the trailhead; LOW: not a route midpoint, OSM has no Settlers Track route and the Parks ACT route map is blocked
namadgi-national-park-7.notes: Source is the Parks ACT self-guided-walk PDF (403 to scripts). Wikivoyage: Brayshaws and Westermans homesteads are mostly visited by those walking the Settlers Track. Walk time unverified. pin LOW.

namadgi-national-park-8.name: Gudgenby Homestead
namadgi-national-park-8.bio: Hut built in 1845 by a Scottish immigrant, dismantled in 1964 and restored, off Boboyan Road.
namadgi-national-park-8.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap node 5039993512 "Gudgenby Homestead No2" (tourism=alpine_hut), MEDIUM; 20 m from the Wikivoyage listing coordinate
namadgi-national-park-8.notes: Wikivoyage: 1.6 km deviation off Boboyan Rd, built 1845, dismantled 1964, timber stored then restored. Placement draft said 'stored for re-erection'; Wikivoyage says restored, so the bio follows it.

namadgi-national-park-9.name: Corin Forest
namadgi-national-park-9.bio: Mountain resort near Tidbinbilla with a 1.2 km alpine slide through Mountain Ash forest and winter snowplay.
namadgi-national-park-9.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap node "Corin Forest Mountain Resort" (tourism=attraction), HIGH; 25 m from Wikivoyage, 33 m from placement
namadgi-national-park-9.notes: Operator site corin.com.au: hours vary by season (2026/27: 9:00-17:00; Sat-Sun only 1 Nov-18 Dec, daily 19 Dec-31 Jan, closed 25 Dec; weekdays closed in much of the year; check before travelling), bookings essential. Alpine slide $30 Youth/Adult (age 8+), from the slide page; snowplay tickets are separate and 2027 bookings not yet open. Visit time is an estimate.

namadgi-national-park-10.name: Tharwa
namadgi-national-park-10.bio: One of the original ACT settlements on the Murrumbidgee, with its old bridge, gateway to Namadgi.
namadgi-national-park-10.coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap place=village node "Tharwa" (Overpass); Commons photo median 187 m away; Wikipedia 434 m
namadgi-national-park-10.notes: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong and Country ACT lists Tharwa Village. Namadgi Visitor Centre is on Naas Rd nearby (Mon-Fri 9-4, Sat-Sun 9-4:30, Wikivoyage Dec 2021), but is a separate place. No single steward: no ticketUrl.
namadgi-national-park-10.ticket_note: A village with no single steward
